title: Nancy Mace recounts prayer meeting and legislative action on social media - Berkeley Leader
text:
U.S. Representative Nancy Mace, who serves South Carolina’s 1st congressional district, shared details of her day on social media, describing interactions with constituents and her role in recent congressional actions.
On February 3, 2026, Mace wrote: “My day began by being prayed over by women who’d traveled from Kentucky and Texas. I spent the afternoon correcting the media’s lies and voting to reopen government. By evening, I found myself face-to-face with a man named ‘Buzz’ who called me a nazi, but we parted ways with a”. The post highlighted encounters throughout her workday.
In a subsequent post on February 4, 2026, she added: “Met this wonderful woman from Kentucky earlier today and she and a friend from Texas prayed over me early this morning. Liberty too! God’s hand at work. https://t.co/MSNleQvzQ3”.
Later that same day, Mace addressed her involvement in efforts related to the release of files connected to Jeffrey Epstein: “Only 4 Republicans had the courage to sign the Epstein petition and force the release of the files. We stood with survivors when the pressure was on. And I’d do it again. No regrets. https://t.co/XPT18HtgNY”.
Nancy Mace has represented South Carolina’s 1st District in Congress since 2021 after succeeding Joe Cunningham (source). Before joining Congress, she served in the South Carolina House of Representatives between 2018 and 2020. Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977, Mace is currently based in Charleston and holds a Bachelor of Science degree from The Citadel (graduated in 1999).
